findings.problem: InvoiceWorkflow uses bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) and a String status instead of enums or a typestate. Any combination of these fields is constructible, including impossible states like status='draft' with is_sent=true, or is_validated=true and is_sent=true simultaneously.
findings.failure_mode: External callers can construct or mutate an invoice into an invalid lifecycle state (e.g., sent but not validated), violating the domain contract. Downstream logic relying on state invariants will silently operate on invalid data.
findings.fix: Replace bool flags and status String with a single InvoiceState enum (e.g., Draft, Validated, Sent) with explicit transitions. Remove is_validated, is_sent, and status as separate fields. Use a typestate or enum to make only valid states constructible.

findings.problem: id and status use raw String primitives instead of domain newtypes like InvoiceId or InvoiceStatus. No domain-level invariants are enforced at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: Any string value is accepted as an invoice ID or status, including empty strings, malformed values, or values from different domains. The compiler cannot distinguish InvoiceWorkflow from other structs that use plain String fields.
findings.fix: Introduce InvoiceId(newtype wrapping a validated String or non-empty type) and replace status String + bool flags with an InvoiceState enum. Parse and validate at the boundary into these trusted types.

findings.problem: All fields of InvoiceWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate id, status, is_validated, and is_sent independently without any state-transition guards.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can bypass mark_sent and directly set is_sent=true while leaving status unchanged, creating an inconsistent object. The struct has no enforced invariants at the type or constructor level.
findings.fix: Make fields private. Provide a private constructor and explicit transition methods (e.g., validate(), mark_sent()) that enforce valid state transitions. Use an internal enum for state.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any InvoiceWorkflow regardless of its current state. It does not check is_validated, reject already-sent invoices, or enforce a valid transition path (e.g., Draft->Validated->Sent).
findings.failure_mode: An invoice can be marked sent without ever being validated, or marked sent multiple times. sent_at_epoch_ms is left as None even after marking sent, producing inconsistent data. This is a silent logic error, not a compile-time or runtime failure.
findings.fix: Replace the free-function mutator with a method on a state-typed InvoiceWorkflow that returns a Result or transitions via an enum pattern. E.g., fn validate(self) -> Result<Self, TransitionError>, fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<Self, TransitionError>. Set sent_at_epoch_ms inside the transition.

findings.problem: InvoiceWorkflow mixes data and behavior. mark_sent is a free function that takes the struct by value and mutates fields, rather than a method with explicit state transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Free-function mutation makes it impossible to attach transition invariants to the type. New callers will naturally add similar free functions, compounding the state-space problem.
findings.fix: Move transition logic into inherent methods on InvoiceWorkflow (or its typestate-wrapped form). The struct becomes inert data; the type system enforces valid transitions.

findings.problem: mark_sent sets is_sent=true and status='sent' but leaves sent_at_epoch_ms as Option<u64> with no assignment. An invoice can appear sent (is_sent=true) without a recorded timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code checking is_sent will find invoices without timestamps, causing nil checks or defaulting to epoch 0. This is a silent data corruption path.
findings.fix: Either require sent_at_epoch_ms as input to mark_sent, or use a clock/clock-provider abstraction in the shell layer to set it during the transition.

residual_risk: The crate has no compile or test gates. The state model is fundamentally broken: any invalid combination of bool flags and String status is constructible and mutable. Without an enum or typestate, no amount of runtime checking can fully prevent illegal states. The review is static only; no commands were run.
